findings.title: Block list lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the address with an exact WHERE email = ? match, and EmailValidator passes the raw attribute through. Signup (User.new_from_params) never downcases or strips the address, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. A blocked row for "bad@spam.com" therefore does not match "Bad@spam.com" or "bad@spam.com ". Changing case is enough to skip the new block and still create the account.

findings.title: Domain allow/deny regex is unanchored and under-escaped
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? only backslash-escapes dots, then compiles /@(#{domains})/i and tests with =~. There is no end anchor, so a whitelist of "company.com" also matches "user@company.com.attacker.com" and the address is allowed. Other regex metacharacters in the site setting (+, *, parentheses, and so on) are interpolated raw, so a crafted or merely punctuation-heavy domain list can change what the check matches or raise RegexpError and fail signup.

findings.title: Block check writes stats non-atomically on every validation
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count in memory and calls save as a side effect of validation, including for action_type :do_nothing. UsersController#create always calls user.valid? and then user.save, and each runs EmailValidator, so one signup attempt counts twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts lose increments. A failure in that save (lock, statement error) aborts registration instead of returning a normal email validation error.

findings.title: Rejected-email cache is case-sensitive and mislabels the error
findings.body: After a failed create, the submitted address is stored in rejectedEmails and later rejected with I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). contains() is case-sensitive, so editing only the case clears the client block and resubmits. The generic "invalid" string also hides the server's blocked/not-allowed reason, which is the only signal the new block list produces.
